text: The feature directory 'flavor-of-day' has no index.ts entry point, so there is no file re-exporting the feature's entire public API — nothing outside the feature can import it, and the Structure rules (exactly one index.ts, types in a dedicated <feature>-types.ts file, verb-first kebab-case logic files) are unmet. The directory must add an index.ts that re-exports the public API (e.g. export { run } from ... / export * from '<feature>-types'), and the 'old-rotation.ts' file is unreachable without it.

The service performs I/O outside the Store: console.log sends output directly instead of mediating all side effects through Store methods. The newsletter delivery must go through a Store method (e.g. store.sendNewsletter or similar) rather than console.log.
Error message 'bad subject' is vague and not actionable for the API consumer; it must name what was wrong and what would be accepted instead (e.g. 'subject must be a non-empty string').

Domain failures must be values, never exceptions. The empty-subject check throws instead of returning { ok: false, error }, so a caller-plausible failure surfaces as an exception; it must return an error result.

The module must export a single entry point named `run` taking the Store first and a single input object, returning a Result<T> from the domain types. This file exports `sendNewsletter` returning boolean; it must export `run(store, input)` yielding a Result<T>.

Every service must have a doc comment stating its purpose in one sentence and enumerating its domain failure modes so a caller can handle every error without reading the body. There is no doc comment here.

The test file frames the unit under test by the feature name 'awards' rather than its module name. The specification's subject-framing rule states the top-level describe must name the unit under test by its module name (e.g. describe('create-review', ...)). The module under test here is the pickWinners module in ../src/features/awards/index.js; the convention appears modeled on naming by module name such as 'create-review', not the feature folder 'awards'. The file must name the top-level describe by the module name of the unit under test. (Note: mechanical naming patterns are out of scope per the judgment boundary, but this is about the semantic framing of the subject, which requires reading comprehension.)

The suite has no nested describe blocks. The single describe is named "newsletter stuff" rather than the module name "send-newsletter", and there are no nested describe("when ...") blocks framing the different situations (valid subject, empty subject, store populated). It must structure tests with nested describes naming each scenario.

Test data is not built inside its test or describe setup to scope each scenario independently. The single test asserts the store ends up containing parlors, but no fresh data setup establishes that state for that assertion; the store is only created and asserted against, mixing observer state with the run. Each scenario (e.g., when subject is empty) must set up its own required data independently rather than relying on the shared single test flow.

The it description is "works", a vague placeholder that does not read with its describe context as a sentence stating one observable outcome. It must describe the specific outcome, e.g. "returns true", "adds a newsletter to the store", "throws an error for an empty subject".

A single it block mixes three distinct outcomes in one block: the return value (toBe(true)), observable store state (store.listParlors().length greater than 0), and an error case (toThrow). These must be separated into distinct it blocks under appropriate nested describes, each with one expect.
